message.content: {"summary":"You earned 29/40. Your strongest work is scenario-specific reasoning in Questions 2 and 4, including a well-applied circuit breaker pattern. To progress, make the availability target measurable, correct the end-to-end calculation in Question 3(c), revise the CAP explanation in Question 5, and include a negative consequence in Question 6.","next_steps":["Revise Questions 1, 3(c), and 5 using explicit measurable targets, the complete end-to-end availability calculation, and the correct CAP interpretation.","Revise Question 6 by adding a specific negative consequence of the durable-queue decision, such as duplicate delivery, delayed notification, or additional queue operations.","Before submitting, check that every answer is within 150 words and that architecture terminology—especially CAP terminology—is precise and consistently supported by IEEE-style citations."],"criteria":{"C1":"In Question 1, you selected and justified suitable performance and availability attributes and used the six-part scenario form. Your performance measure is measurable, but “stay up most of the time” is not. State a target such as a percentage availability or maximum monthly downtime to reach Excellent.","C2":"Your modular-monolith recommendation in Question 2 is excellent: you link trade-offs to the five-person team, the single-VM problem, and deployment downtime, and acknowledge limited independent scaling and shared-process failure. Maintain this scenario-specific justification.","C3":"Parts (a) and (b) in Question 3 are correctly calculated and rounded. In part (c), do not report the redundant payment-provider figure as end-to-end availability. Include all components and report approximately 99.80% availability and 1.5 hours of monthly downtime, with working, to reach Excellent.","C4":"Question 4 is excellent. You accurately explain circuit-breaker states, apply the pattern to the slow payment provider, and give a relevant threshold and time window for tuning. Continue connecting the mechanism, outage, user impact, and operational consideration this specifically.","C5":"Your choices in Question 5 are reasonable and you name concrete techniques. Correct the CAP statement: during a partition, a system must choose consistency or availability; it cannot give up partition tolerance. Also explain that an idempotency key prevents duplicate retries but does not ensure consistency across a partition.","C6":"Question 6 includes specific Context, Decision, and Consequences sections, and the durable queue decision is clear. Add at least one negative consequence—such as duplicate delivery, delayed notification, or extra queue operations—alongside the benefits to reach Excellent.","C7":"Your headings, clear writing, citations, and broadly IEEE-style reference list are strengths. To reach Excellent, verify every answer is within 150 words and use precise terminology throughout, particularly the CAP explanation in Question 5."}}
